title: Zenzap: The agent has joined the work conversation
gist: Bessemer's Adam Fisher announces the public launch of portfolio company Zenzap, a mobile-native work chat where employee-built, role-based AI agents live in group chats connected to 400+ apps. He argues personal agents will repeat WhatsApp's shadow-IT pattern, so firms need a sanctioned, governed agent platform now, citing 60% daily usage and ~20x activity growth two weeks after rollout.

themes.theme: Agents move from personal to multiplayer

insights.claim: Bessemer argues the first wave of AI was personal, but business agents must be multiplayer because work happens across people, teams, tools and approvals.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Enterprise agent value accrues to platforms that coordinate many users and agents, not single-user assistants.
insights.quote: The first wave of AI was personal, but businesses don’t work like individuals. Work happens across people, teams, tools, and approvals.

insights.claim: According to Bessemer, the key enterprise AI question has shifted from which model to use to where agents live, what they can access, how employees reach them, and how IT controls them.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Model choice is commoditizing; distribution surface, access and governance become the competitive battleground.
insights.quote: The question changed from which model to use to where agents should live, what they can access, how every employee reaches them, and how IT keeps them under control.

insights.claim: Bessemer contrasts consumer agents, a single super-agent acting as the user's alter ego, with business agents that run on roles, each with its own skills and tool access.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Role-based, specialized agent architectures may fit enterprise workflows better than one general assistant.
insights.quote: Consumer agents are a single super-agent that acts as your alter ego. Think of business agents as multiplayer.
insights.locator: Consumer agents are a single super-agent

insights.claim: Bessemer claims employees today act as the human integration layer, leaving chat to check calendars, update the CRM and pull numbers before reporting back, and that Zenzap brings that work into the conversation instead.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Chat surfaces that absorb cross-app tasks could displace context switching and point-integration tools.
insights.quote: The employee is the integration layer. On Zenzap, the work comes to the conversation.
insights.locator: Think of an employee who reads

insights.claim: On Zenzap, agents sit in group chats as teammates connected to more than 400 business apps, pulling data into threads, acting, obtaining approvals and writing results back.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Breadth of integrations (400+) is a core part of the product moat claim.
insights.quote: Agents live in group chats as teammates, connected to more than 400 business apps.
insights.locator: Think of an employee who reads

insights.claim: In a clinic example, a Zenzap agent detects a patient cancellation and posts it in the reception channel, where a receptionist claims and fills the slot.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Healthcare front-office workflows are an early vertical use case for chat-native agents.
insights.quote: Even in a clinic setting, an agent picks up a patient’s cancellation and posts it in the reception channel
insights.locator: Consumer agents are a single super-agent

insights.claim: Zenzap was founded three years ago by Guy Weiss, Jonatan Bien and Noam Neumann as mobile-native work chat, as intuitive as WhatsApp but governed like Slack, which Bessemer backed from inception despite messaging being seen as a solved market.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Bessemer frames a pre-agentic messaging bet as now repositioned as an agent distribution layer.
insights.quote: It was a contrarian bet, since most of tech considered messaging a solved market.
insights.locator: Some companies get lucky with timing

themes.theme: Employee-built agents and the long tail

insights.claim: Bessemer argues the best enterprise agents will be built by frontline employees rather than IT, because IT can automate obvious workflows but cannot see the long tail where most value sits.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: No-code, bottom-up agent creation could capture value that centralized IT automation programs miss.
insights.quote: IT can automate the obvious workflows, but it can never see the long tail, and that’s where most of the value sits.
insights.locator: IT can automate the obvious workflows

insights.claim: Any Zenzap employee can create an agent in under 90 seconds with no code and no training.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Very low creation friction is the mechanism behind the bottom-up adoption thesis.
insights.quote: any employee can create an agent in under 90 seconds, with no code and no training.
insights.locator: With Zenzap, any employee can create

insights.claim: Bessemer notes that a vast majority of the workforce, such as restaurant managers, construction crews and hotel staff, never adopted Slack, positioning mobile chat as the route to deskless workers.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Deskless workers are an underpenetrated market for both workplace chat and AI agents.
insights.quote: A vast majority of the workforce, from restaurant managers to construction crews to hotel staff, never adopted Slack in the first place
insights.locator: IT can automate the obvious workflows

themes.theme: Shadow AI repeats the WhatsApp pattern

insights.claim: Bessemer predicts personal agents will repeat the shadow-IT pattern of WhatsApp, only faster, and will not just carry company information but act on it.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Ungoverned agent use is a looming security and compliance risk, creating demand for sanctioned agent platforms.
insights.quote: Personal agents are about to repeat that pattern, only faster, and this time they won’t just carry company information; they’ll act on it.
insights.locator: Personal agents are about to repeat

insights.claim: Bessemer observes that employees moved work to WhatsApp without IT approval, so customer details, invoices and patient updates now flow through personal accounts companies cannot see or control.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Precedent suggests employees adopt useful tools before IT, so vendors offering a sanctioned alternative early can win.
insights.quote: They moved work to WhatsApp, and today, customer details, invoices, and patient updates flow through personal accounts the company can’t see or control.

insights.claim: Bessemer warns that companies that fail to give employees a sanctioned way to build agents now will find personal agents already handling their work.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: The adoption window for enterprise agent platforms is framed as short and urgent.
insights.quote: Companies that don’t give employees a sanctioned way to build agents now will soon find personal agents already handling their work.
insights.locator: Personal agents are about to repeat

insights.claim: Each Zenzap agent runs in its own isolated computer per conversation, never holds credentials, routes every request through a firewall it cannot control, requires human approval for actions like sending invoices, and logs everything.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Sandboxing, credential isolation and human-in-the-loop approvals are emerging as the enterprise agent security baseline.
insights.quote: Each agent runs in its own isolated computer for every conversation, never holds credentials, and sends every request through a firewall it can’t control.

insights.claim: Zenzap has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit, is GDPR compliant, supports HIPAA under a BAA, and offers EU or US data residency and BYOK.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Compliance credentials enable selling into regulated sectors like healthcare.
insights.quote: Zenzap has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit, is GDPR compliant, supports HIPAA under a BAA, and offers EU or US data residency and BYOK.

insights.claim: Two weeks after Zenzap agents rolled out to existing customers, 60% of those who enabled them use them daily, having set them up entirely on their own.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: High self-serve daily usage suggests product-led adoption, though the base and sample are undisclosed.
insights.quote: 60% of those who switched them on now use them daily, having set them up entirely on their own.
insights.locator: Two weeks after Zenzap agents rolled

insights.claim: Zenzap agent activity grew roughly 20x in the two weeks after rollout, and one clinic recovered $1,583 in missed payments on its first day.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Early engagement growth and concrete ROI anecdotes support the thesis but are from a very short window.
insights.quote: Agent activity grew roughly 20x in that time. One clinic recovered $1,583 in missed payments on its first day.
insights.locator: Two weeks after Zenzap agents rolled

insights.claim: Zenzap launched publicly on Oct 14, 2026 with thousands of businesses already running on it.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: An existing customer base gives the agent product an immediate distribution channel.
insights.quote: Today, Zenzap launches publicly, with thousands of businesses already running on it.

insights.claim: Bessemer argues that, unlike past cycles where businesses waited years after consumers for a trustworthy version, enterprises can now adopt agents at the same time as consumers.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Enterprise agent adoption may not lag consumer adoption as previous technology waves did.
insights.quote: Consumers usually get the new thing first, and businesses wait years for a version they can trust. This time, they don’t have to.
insights.locator: Consumers usually get the new thing
